newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, edging toward overbought.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, edging toward overbought.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer, building on gains from earlier in the week which propelled the most-active contract to its highest point since just before Sumitomo's announcement of huge losses caused prices to slide.
"The market looks close to being overbought, but it does certainly appear there is still considerable upside potential," John Gross of the Copper Journal said.
Copper inventories were at low levels, he added.
Most-active COMEX July copper has moved into uncharted territory, setting a new life-of-contract high of 118.85 cents, the second fresh high this week.
July settled 0.35 cent firmer at 118.20 cents per pound, traded 118.85 to 117.50 cents. Spot May went out 0.45 cent higher at 118.55 cents. Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots.
LME stocks fell 1,125 tonnes to 139,975 tonnes Wednesday.
Brokers noted that much of the LME stocks were now in expensive or out of the way locations such as Long Beach, Helsinborg, and Bilbao.
Some of the LME stocks in Long Beach were from COMEX.
"COMEX stocks have been coming down and that's more of a reflection of consumption because the arbitrage in May did not allow for delivery of COMEX metal to Long Beach," a broker said.
COMEX stocks stood Wednesday at 39,373 short tons, down from some 50,000 short tons a few weeks ago.
